children: video game launched on Tuesday as a single-player, third-person action-adventure exclusive to the Sony
PlayStation 5. Insomniac Games developed it for Sony Interactive Entertainment in collaboration with Marvel Games.
Wolverine’s game legacy predates the release by decades. He first appeared in 1989’s The Uncanny X-Men on Nintendo

and later received an NES solo title, Wolverine, in 1991. He also became a regular playable figure in ensemble series such as X-Men Legends, Marvel: Ultimate Alliance, and fighting games. The original story casts Logan as a violent but vulnerable hero confronting threats to mutants while pursuing answers about his own past across Canada, Tokyo, and Madripoor.

For investors, the release is strategically important for Sony, which owns Insomniac and publishes the game. Insomniac benefits as the creator of another marquee Marvel property after its Marvel’s Spider-Man games, while Marvel Games and parent company Disney
benefit from licensing revenue and renewed consumer attention around the Wolverine/X-Men brand.

is reportedly a major hit with PS5 players, with strong early download activity and positive player reviews on Metacritic. Critical reviews are mixed, with Game Informer raving about the "intense and unrelenting ride" and GameSpot calling it at best a fun but forgettable experience.
